Subject: Performance SLO qualification — post-call recap and next steps

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and suggested next steps so we can align on the perf run: 

Key FinCo requirements (from today):
- Latency: target p95 <= 200ms for short-turn QA responses (<= 256 output tokens). For longer generations (>= 512 output tokens) acceptable p95 up to 600ms with streaming enabled.
- Throughput: baseline 150 QPS sustained, spike to 300 QPS for 5–10 minute windows.
- Concurrency: expected 40–60 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Context window: typical request will include ~6k input tokens (customer history + metadata), can spike to 8k; expected output up to 1k tokens.
- Streaming: required for longer responses to surface partial tokens within 200–300ms of generation start.

Implications we covered:
- Larger context windows (6k–8k) increase per-request KV cache reads and can raise tail latency; with our optimizations we expect ~1.2–1.8x token-processing overhead vs. 2k-window.
- Batching improves throughput but can increase latency for single-user interactive flows; for FinCo we recommended a hybrid: route interactive traffic to low-batch nodes (autobatch max latency 100ms) and batch background inference.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency for long outputs but requires websocket/streaming support in the client and a persistent connection — we confirmed FinCo is ok with that.

Action items / next steps:
1) We will provision a dedicated perf pool that mirrors your target config (8x A100-equivalent GPUs, reserved concurrency 60) and run two tests: (A) interactive profile (single-turn, low-batch, streaming) and (B) throughput profile (high-batch, sustained QPS).
2) FinCo to confirm representative prompt set (please share 10–20 example requests covering short, medium, long outputs).
3) Procurement to confirm timing/PO/any redlines — cc'd procurement@finco.com.
4) We will share a short SLO table and demo recording (attached) and follow up with test schedule.

Attached: FinCo_SLO_requirements_v1.xlsx (SLO table), demo-recording-20270318.mp4

If the above looks right I’ll schedule the perf run for next Tue/Wed (Mar 23–24) and send an access link for the streaming websocket.

—

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — streaming + context window notes

Tom — quick technical notes to answer your questions and set expectations for the perf run: 
1) Streaming model behavior: yes — we provide chunked partial outputs with explicit sequence numbers on each chunk. Ordering is stable; we also surface 'is_final' for the last chunk so the client can safely stitch. We typically guarantee first-chunk latency within 200–300ms under interactive routing.
2) KV cache & context window: with an 8k input window we expect per-request memory access and attention overhead to increase. Practically, on our A100-equivalent nodes we've observed p95 add of ~150–350ms vs. 2k-window for generation-heavy prompts. That delta depends on tokenization (avg tokens per char) and whether requests hit prefix caches.
3) Batching strategy: for the interactive lane we will use micro-batches (batch size 1–4) with priority scheduling; throughput lane will use larger batches to hit the QPS target. This hybrid keeps interactive p95 near your 200ms target for short outputs.
4) Cost delta (rough): dedicated perf pool (reserved) is typically ~1.4–1.7x the cost of equivalent hosted autoscale during heavy, sustained usage due to reserved capacity pricing and priority routing. We'll put a line-item in the SLO spreadsheet with a worked example.

Next step from our side: I’ll coordinate with infra to spin up the perf pool on Monday night and run an initial smoke test Tue morning. Marissa — can you confirm Tom's prompt set arrival and whether FinCo wants the websocket auth via JWT or temporary API keys?

—
